summary.en: Meet the famous yogas, the combinations that give a chart its themes, and see doshas in calm balance.

outcome.en: spot the main yogas and talk about doshas without fear

question.en: Mangal sits in Makara in the 10th house from the lagna. Which yoga does this form?

explanation.en: Mangal is exalted in Makara, and the 10th is a kendra. A Mahapurusha graha in its own or exalted sign in a kendra from the lagna gives Ruchaka.

question.en: For a Vrishabha lagna, why is Shani called the yogakaraka?

options.en: It rules the 9th and 10th, a trikona and a kendra

explanation.en: From Vrishabha, Makara is the 9th (a trikona) and Kumbha the 10th (a kendra). One graha ruling both is a yogakaraka, a raja yoga in itself.

body.en: In Jyotish, a yoga (combination) is a pattern of placements that joins grahas, signs and houses into one theme. The word comes from yuj, to join. A yoga describes a theme in the chart, not a fixed event.

The classics describe hundreds of yogas. Parashara, Varahamihira and Mantreswara each give their own sets, and the names and rules sometimes differ. You don't need them all: a few famous ones teach the logic behind the rest.

Some yogas turn up in a large share of charts. Gaja Kesari needs only Guru in a kendra from the Moon, which happens in roughly one chart in three. Having a famous yoga is pleasant, but it is rarely rare.

A yoga gives results in proportion to the strength of the grahas that form it. Dignity, house, aspects and combustion all count. A yoga made by weak or troubled grahas tends to give a mild or partial result.
Yogas tend to show their themes most in the dasha or antardasha of the grahas that form them. A yoga can rest quietly for years and come forward when its graha's period begins.
No single yoga decides a life. Good teachers weigh each yoga against the rest of the kundli, and against effort and free will. Treat a yoga as a theme to explore, never as a promise or a threat.

question.en: What does the word yoga mean in a kundli?

options.en: A breathing practice for each graha
A combination that joins placements into a theme
A graha sitting alone in a house

explanation.en: From yuj, to join: a yoga joins grahas, signs and houses into one theme in the chart.

question.en: What mostly decides how strongly a yoga works?

options.en: The strength of the grahas that form it
How rare the yoga's name sounds

explanation.en: A yoga is only as strong as its grahas: their dignity, house, aspects and freedom from combustion.

question.en: When does a yoga tend to show its themes most?

options.en: In the dasha of the grahas that form it

explanation.en: Dashas time a chart's promises. A yoga usually comes forward in the periods of the grahas that make it.

body.en: The Pancha Mahapurusha yogas are the five 'great person' yogas. Each belongs to one of the five true planets: Mangal, Budha, Guru, Shukra and Shani. The Sun, Moon, Rahu and Ketu don't form them.

The yoga forms when one of these grahas sits in its own sign or its exaltation sign, and that sign is a kendra: house 1, 4, 7 or 10 from the lagna. A strong graha in a strong house gives a clear, lasting theme.

Ruchaka forms with Mangal in Mesha or Vrishchika (own signs) or Makara (exalted) in a kendra. It tends to bring courage, drive, energy and a leader's push. Channelled well, it is the athlete or the protector.

Bhadra forms with Budha in Mithuna or Kanya in a kendra. Kanya is both Budha's own sign and its exaltation. It tends to give a quick mind, skill with words and numbers, wit, and a gift for trade or teaching.

Hamsa forms with Guru in Dhanu or Meena (own signs) or Karka (exalted) in a kendra. The hamsa is the swan, a symbol of discernment. It tends to give wisdom, goodness, a teaching spirit and the respect of others.

Malavya: Shukra in Vrishabha, Tula or Meena (exalted) in a kendra; it tends to give grace, art and comfort. Shasha: Shani in Makara, Kumbha or Tula (exalted) in a kendra; it tends to give discipline, endurance and slowly earned authority.

Your lagna is {value}. Count it as 1, then find the 4th, 7th and 10th signs: those are your kendras. A Mahapurusha yoga needs Mangal, Budha, Guru, Shukra or Shani in its own or exalted sign in one of them.

unknownTime.en: Mahapurusha yogas are counted from the lagna, which needs a birth time. Some teachers also look from the Moon sign, so you can still explore these yogas from your Chandra rashi.

explanation.en: Hamsa belongs to Guru: Jupiter in Dhanu, Meena or Karka in a kendra from the lagna.

question.en: Shani is in Tula in the 7th house from the lagna. Which yoga is this?

explanation.en: Shani is exalted in Tula and the 7th is a kendra, so this is Shasha. Tula is Shukra's sign, but Malavya needs Shukra itself there.

question.en: Why can't Surya form a Mahapurusha yoga?

options.en: Only the five true planets, Mangal to Shani, form them
Surya never sits in a kendra

explanation.en: The five yogas belong to Mangal, Budha, Guru, Shukra and Shani. The Sun and Moon (the luminaries) and Rahu and Ketu are left out.

body.en: Recall the two strongest house groups. Kendras (1, 4, 7, 10) are the pillars of action. Trikonas (1, 5, 9) are the houses of fortune and dharma. The lagna is both, which is why its lord matters so much.

A raja yoga (royal combination) forms when a kendra lord and a trikona lord come together: in the same sign, by mutual aspect, or by exchanging signs. It tends to bring status, responsibility and recognition in one's own field.
When one graha rules both a kendra and a trikona, it is a yogakaraka. Classic examples: Shani for Vrishabha and Tula lagnas, Mangal for Karka and Simha, and Shukra for Makara and Kumbha.

Meera has Karka lagna. Mangal rules her 5th and 10th, so it is her yogakaraka. Mangal sits exalted in Makara, her 7th, which also makes Ruchaka. Purposeful work and standing tend to be strong themes, most of all in Mangal's dasha.

A dhana yoga (wealth combination) links the lords of the 2nd and 11th, the houses of savings and gains, with the lords of the trikonas 1, 5 and 9. It points to a theme of earning and resources, often through one's own skill.

A dhana yoga is never a promise of riches, and its absence is no sign of hardship. Effort, choices and circumstances shape money far more. For real money decisions, talk to a qualified financial adviser, not a chart.

question.en: Which pairing forms a raja yoga?

options.en: The lords of the 6th and 8th joining
The lords of the 3rd and 11th joining
The lords of the 4th and 9th joining

explanation.en: The 4th is a kendra and the 9th a trikona. Their lords joining, aspecting each other or exchanging signs is a raja yoga.

question.en: For a Tula lagna, which graha is the yogakaraka?

explanation.en: From Tula, Makara is the 4th (kendra) and Kumbha the 5th (trikona). Shani rules both. Shukra rules the 1st and 8th instead.

question.en: What does a dhana yoga in a chart mean?

options.en: A theme of earning and resources, not a promise
Wealth guaranteed by a certain age
That gold should be bought in its dasha

explanation.en: Yogas describe themes. A dhana yoga points to resources and gains, while effort and choices shape what actually happens.

body.en: Gaja Kesari means 'elephant and lion'. It forms when Guru sits in a kendra from Chandra: in the Moon's own sign, or the 4th, 7th or 10th sign from it. It tends to give good sense, dignity and a respected name.

Guru is in a kendra from the Moon in about one chart in three, so Gaja Kesari is common. Classical texts add conditions, such as Guru not being debilitated, combust or in an enemy's sign. A strong Guru gives a fuller result.
Your Moon is in {value}. Count that sign as 1, then find Guru in your kundli. If Guru sits in the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th sign from your Moon, you have Gaja Kesari; next, see how strong Guru is.

Budha-Aditya forms when Budha joins Surya (Aditya, the Sun) in one sign. It tends to give intelligence, clear speech and a love of learning. Many texts name it, and students of Jyotish are fond of it.

Budha never strays more than about 28° from the Sun, so the two share a sign in a large share of charts. Many teachers add that Budha should not be too close to the Sun, or it is combust (asta) and the yoga gives less.
Common yogas are still real themes; they just don't make anyone special or lacking. A chart without Gaja Kesari can have a strong Guru elsewhere, and many wise people have neither yoga.

question.en: Gaja Kesari forms when Guru is…

options.en: In a kendra from the Moon

explanation.en: Guru in the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th sign from Chandra gives Gaja Kesari.

question.en: Why is Budha-Aditya yoga so common?

options.en: Budha is exalted in every sign
The Sun changes sign every week
Budha always stays close to the Sun

explanation.en: Budha is never more than about 28° from the Sun, so it often shares the Sun's sign.

question.en: Ravi's Moon is in Simha and his Guru is in Vrishchika. Does he have Gaja Kesari?

options.en: No, Guru must sit with the Moon
Yes, Guru is 4th from his Moon
No, Guru is 8th from his Moon

explanation.en: Count Simha as 1: Kanya 2, Tula 3, Vrishchika 4. The 4th is a kendra from the Moon, so the yoga forms.

body.en: A dosha (blemish) is a combination the tradition flags for care. Like yogas, doshas are themes, not sentences. Each has conditions that soften or cancel it, called bhanga (cancellation), and most charts have one or another.

Mangal dosha, or being 'manglik', is traditionally Mangal in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th house. Definitions vary: some leave out the 1st or 2nd, and some also count from the Moon and Shukra. It concerns the energy brought into partnership.

Six houses out of twelve means roughly half of all charts are manglik by the common rule, and more if you count from the Moon and Shukra too. Something so common can't be a mark against anyone. It simply describes a lively, direct Mangal.

Texts and teachers list many cancellations: Mangal in its own sign or exalted, Guru's aspect on Mangal, both partners having it, and more. Teachers accept different rules, so a careful reading looks at the whole chart.
Mangal dosha is never a reason to blame, reject or shame anyone, and never a reason to fear marriage. Respect and good communication matter far more. No paid ritual is needed to 'fix' a chart.

Kemadruma is when no graha (leaving out the Sun, Rahu and Ketu) sits in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon. It is linked with feeling alone at times. It is often cancelled, for example by a graha in a kendra from the Moon or the lagna.

question.en: Roughly how many charts are manglik by the common rule?

options.en: Only people born on a Tuesday

explanation.en: Mangal in 6 of the 12 houses makes about half of all charts manglik, which is why it should never alarm anyone.

question.en: Which of these is a traditional cancellation of Mangal dosha?

explanation.en: When both partners are manglik, tradition treats the dosha as cancelled. Mangal in its own or exalted sign is another common cancellation.

question.en: Kemadruma is counted from which graha?

explanation.en: Kemadruma looks at the 2nd and 12th signs from Chandra, the Moon, and has many cancellations.
